summary: The note describes the rise of the gig economy and freelance work as a lasting shift away from traditional 9-to-5 employment, citing a GFA report and BLE data that about 36% of the U.S. workforce does freelance or gig work. It covers economic effects on businesses, personal growth, diversity and inclusivity, and technology's role, illustrated with quotes from freelancers and executives. It closes by noting ongoing debates over healthcare, retirement benefits and employment rights for freelancers.
one_line: The gig economy and freelancing are reshaping labor markets, businesses and careers, with about 36% of the U.S. workforce involved, as of November 2023.
key_facts: The gig economy is a labor market defined by short-term contracts or freelance work rather than permanent jobs; workers are paid per 'gig' such as food delivery or ridesharing.
The Global Freelancers Association (GFA) released a report on October 5, 2023 saying the gig economy is burgeoning and reshaping career perspectives.
GFA spokesperson Anne Cummings said 'more people than ever are choosing to go freelance, valuing the flexibility to work when, where, and how they like.'
According to the Bureau of Labor and Economics (BLE), as of November 2023 roughly 36% of the U.S. workforce is involved in freelance or gig work.
Johnathan Millard left his corporate job to become a full-time freelance graphic designer in December 2023.
On January 15, 2024, Emily Torres, CEO of TechFin Innovations, said employing freelance experts on a project basis keeps the company agile and innovative, and is cost-effective.
Michael Jenkins, a freelance digital marketer, said on February 20, 2024 that going freelance expanded his portfolio and forced him to learn and adapt quickly.
Sarah Langdon, an independent IT consultant, said in March 2024 that being her own boss means constantly learning about running a business.
Julie Gomis, a freelance content writer based in Senegal, said the freelance model has democratized the job market, letting talent shine irrespective of location.
Tech analyst Robert Mahoney said anyone with a skill and internet access can potentially build a career online with modern tools and platforms.
Freelancers must manage every aspect of their business, building time management, negotiation skills and financial literacy.
Debates continue over healthcare, retirement benefits and employment rights for freelancers.
